correctness.rationale: A finite Boolean powerset homomorphism h:P([m])->P([n]) maps every atom to one block of a partition of [n], so h=f^{-1} for a function f:[n]->[m]. Preserving the global quorum threshold requires |S|>=ell iff sum_{i in S}|f^{-1}(i)|>=k for every S. If some fiber were empty, an (ell-1)-set missing that coordinate and the same set with the empty coordinate added force contradictory truth values; thus f is surjective. With positive fibers the inequalities reduce exactly to sum of ell smallest >=k and sum of ell-1 largest <k. Robin-Hood balancing weakly raises smallest partial sums and lowers largest, proving the stated quotient-remainder existence criterion; multinomial assignment of integer partitions gives the hom-set count. For n=m, surjective maps are permutations, so every endomorphism is an automorphism and only identity is idempotent. At n=qm, strict deviation of upper/lower partial sums from their balanced averages forces equal fibers at quota endpoints; for q>=3 the profile (q-1,q,...,q,q+1) works at each nonempty interior quota. Independently direct-enumerated all function fiber criteria n<=5 for every quota and q=3,m=3,n=9 count vector 1680,11130,1680; the universal proof is algebraic, not this finite test.

originality.rationale: Classical Stone/powerset and monotone-neighborhood dualities establish the inverse-image/function correspondence (prior, not novel). A full hom-set criterion for uniform quotas, the optimal balanced existence interval, exact sum over fiber partitions, and the endpoint/interior rigidity transition jointly specialize this general framework; a general categorical duality alone does not give these arithmetic formulas. Weighted majority voting representation studies discuss quotas and weight profiles, but consulted papers concern game representation frequencies and optimization, not preserving a source threshold through a surjective fiber expansion between two finite uniform-threshold algebras. Best-of-knowledge no identical result recovered.
